text:
lucy: noticed a small but noisy eviction spike this morning during a tenant rollout. tracing shows clients accepted an update before the control plane committed, GC evicted, fallback to slower variant.
ben: classic race. our pin TTL doesn't express in-flight commit state. clients only see ttl/last_updated.
arya: proposal: add a tiny lease block to rollout metadata: `lease_seq` (monotonic int), `commit_state` enum {"provisional","durable"}, `commit_ts_ms` (ms int), and `grace_ms` (int). keep wire values as ms ints.
lucy: how would clients behave?
ben: if commit_state=="provisional" then clients allow cached pin only while now < commit_ts_ms + grace_ms AND cached lease_seq == lease_seq. otherwise re-resolve. if absent fields, default to durable/0 for compatibility.
arya: tradeoffs: small metadata size, no crypto tokens to manage. downside: less cryptographic guarantee — but we can add `commit_sig` later if needed.
infra-bot: metric suggestions: provisional_use_count, provisional_mismatch_count, provisional_transition_latency. ops: add dashboard and alert if provisional->durable > 5s.
deploy-bot: recommend read-only emit for 7 days, SDK updates next, then GC semantics behind feature flag for 5% cohort. schedule canary window after SDKs land.
lucy: tests: batched renewals with 0-5s delay, client clock skew +/-3s, and chaos test injecting many provisional states.
ben: backward compatibility: clients must treat missing block as commit_state="durable". keep helpers in SDKs (go/python/node) called isCachedPinValid(cached, server, now_ms).
arya: i'll open the RFC PR with schema examples, migration notes, and acceptance criteria. thanks all :thumbsup:
